cards.html:
Peptides your body makes

Your gut has a stop-eating peptide.

Fig. 1 · Meet CCK

Cholecys­tokinin

Made by I cells in your upper small intestine.

Fig. 2 · The trigger

Fat and protein arrive.

Your gut releases CCK into the blood.

Fig. 3 · What CCK does
1Gallbladder squeezes: bile out
2Pancreas releases enzymes
3Stomach empties slower

Fig. 4 · The fullness signal

Gut → vagus nerve → brain

The message: “that's enough.”

Fig. 5 · History

1928

Named for moving the gallbladder.

1973

First hormone shown to cut meal size (in rats).

Save this for your physiology exam.
